title: Council calls for more financial adviser scrutiny
full_text:
Financial advisers would face heavier scrutiny under a beefed-up supervision program emboldening the corporate cop to probe advice licensees twice yearly.
That is the proposal put forward by the Financial Services Council, which is also proposing licensees be hit with a hefty $25,000 annual bill to fund the new supervision-led regulatory oversight. The FSC is calling for ASIC’s “set-and-forget” approach to advice licensees to be abandoned in favour of biannual supervisory engagement with every licensee, according to its recommendations. It comes in the wake of the Shield Master Fund and First Guardian Master Fund failures, two investment schemes that took in $1bn of client money before collapsing into liquidation in the past 18 months.
Almost all the money invested in the two funds was done so on the recommendations of financial advisers, many of which have either been banned by ASIC or are under investigation. The regulator is also suing advice licensee Interprac Financial Planning, alleging critical oversight and compliance failures.
“ASIC must be equipped with the information, resources and supervisory capability to identify and address risks before consumers suffer harm,” FSC says.
